text: Leaning on his elbow. <break time="0.8s" /> Gabriel looked, without resentment. <break time="0.8s" /> At her tangled hair and half open mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> And it hardly pained him now. <break time="0.8s" /> To think. <break time="0.8s" /> How poor a part he, her husband. <break time="0.8s" /> Had played in her life. <break time="0.8s" /> He watched her. <break time="0.8s" /> As though they had never lived together. <break time="0.8s" /> As man and wife. <break time="0.8s" /> And as he thought of what she must have been in her first girlish beauty. <break time="0.8s" /> A strange, friendly pity for her. <break time="0.8s" /> Entered his soul. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon, he thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Poor Aunt Julia would also become a shade. <break time="0.8s" /> And it seemed better. <break time="0.8s" /> To pass boldly into that other world. <break time="0.8s" /> In the full glory of some passion. <break time="0.8s" /> Than to fade and wither dismally with age. <break time="0.8s" /> Generous tears filled his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> For although he had never felt like that himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Toward any woman. <break time="0.8s" /> He knew. <break time="0.8s" /> That such a feeling must be love. <break time="0.8s" /> In the partial darkness. <break time="0.8s" /> He imagined he saw the form. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a young man. <break time="0.8s" /> Standing under a dripping tree. <break time="0.8s" /> And his soul approached that region. <break time="0.8s" /> Where dwell the vast hosts of the dead. <break time="0.8s" /> His own identity was fading out. <break time="0.8s" /> Into a grey, impalpable world. <break time="0.8s" /> Until a few light taps upon the pane. <break time="0.8s" /> Made him turn and see the snow. <break time="0.8s" /> Silver and dark. <break time="0.8s" /> Falling obliquely against the lamplight. <break time="0.8s" /> The time had come for him. <break time="0.8s" /> To set out on his journey westward. <break time="0.8s" /> And snow was general all over Ireland. <break time="0.8s" /> Falling softly upon the Bog of Allen. <break time="0.8s" /> And, further westward. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the dark mutinous Shannon waves. <break time="0.8s" /> It lay thickly drifted. <break time="0.8s" /> On the crooked crosses of the lonely churchyard. <break time="0.8s" /> Where Michael Furey lay buried. <break time="0.8s" /> And his soul swooned slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> As he heard the snow falling faintly. <break time="0.8s" /> Through the universe and faintly falling. <break time="0.8s" /> Upon all the living and the dead.
